title: Responsive and adaptive layouts: what to check in each

videos.script: A phone and a laptop open the same shop. They do not always get the same page. {{two}} There are two ways to make that happen. A responsive page is one page, and its stylesheet fits it to the window. An adaptive page is chosen by the server, from the name the browser gives itself. {{viewport}} A test can pretend to be either. Playwright sets the width of the window, the density of its pixels, touch, and that name. {{breakpoints}} For the responsive shop, you test both sides of each line in the stylesheet. At six hundred pixels the links hide behind a Menu button. At six hundred and one they come back. {{overflow}} Then the check a robot does best. Does anything make the page scroll sideways? On a phone three hundred and sixty pixels wide, the shop does, by forty pixels. {{adaptive}} For the adaptive page, the width decides nothing. Same width, a different name, a different page. {{limits}} And pretending has limits. A Chromium that calls itself an iPhone is still Chromium. It is not Safari, and it is not a phone in your hand. {{checklist}} The lesson ends with what to check in each kind, and what to leave to a person.
